candidates.name: Endothelial-friendly surface coating (heparin / CD47 / phosphorylcholine / polydopamine)
candidates.core_mechanism: Apply a biocompatible coating to the eShunt's outer surface where it contacts venous sinus endothelium and jugular vein. Coating inhibits platelet adhesion, complement activation, and endothelial denudation.
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: Heparin catalyzes antithrombin III; CD47 emits 'don't eat me' signal; phosphorylcholine mimics cell membrane; polydopamine enables biofunctionalization.
candidates.credibility: HIGH — these coatings are well-established on vascular stents and clinically deployed
candidates.credibility_concern: HIGHLY SATURATED — drug-eluting stent coatings are standard of care. No eShunt-specific novelty on coating chemistry alone.

candidates.name: Flow-distributing stent geometry (reduce wall shear stress gradients on venous sinus wall)
candidates.core_mechanism: Design the eShunt's outer scaffold geometry to redistribute venous blood flow around the eShunt body, minimizing wall shear stress gradients at the venous interface and preventing stagnation zones behind the eShunt.
candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Intimal hyperplasia from disturbed flow (WSS gradients), stagnation-induced thrombosis
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: WSS = 6μQ/(πhr²) for annular flow; geometric struts can route flow to avoid low-WSS recirculation pockets; established in flow-diverter stent literature.
candidates.credibility: HIGH — flow-diverting stents well-established for aneurysms; WSS gradients known to drive IH (Malek 1999)
candidates.credibility_concern: MEDIUM saturation — flow diverters established for ARTERIAL aneurysms (goal: STAGNATE flow for thrombosis). eShunt-specific application to VENOUS drainage (goal: AVOID stagnation) is OPPOSITE-direction mechanism, requiring §103 distinction.

candidates.name: Drug-eluting anti-proliferative sleeve (paclitaxel / everolimus / zotarolimus)
candidates.core_mechanism: Polymeric sleeve on eShunt outer surface that elutes anti-proliferative drugs (limus-family or paclitaxel) at the venous interface over 30-90 days to inhibit smooth muscle proliferation and intimal hyperplasia.
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: Limus drugs inhibit mTOR; paclitaxel stabilizes microtubules. Both prevent smooth muscle cell proliferation at drug-eluting stent contact sites.
candidates.credibility: HIGH — drug-eluting stents are the standard of care for coronary arteries
candidates.credibility_concern: HIGHLY SATURATED — DES is a $5B+ market with hundreds of patents (Abbott, Medtronic, Boston Scientific). eShunt-specific novelty on elution profile alone is weak.

candidates.name: Endothelial progenitor cell (EPC) seeding — living interface
candidates.core_mechanism: Pre-seed eShunt's outer surface with autologous or allogeneic endothelial progenitor cells before deployment, creating a living interface that integrates with venous endothelium.
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: EPCs (CD34+ cells) capture on antibody-coated stent surfaces, differentiate into mature endothelial cells, and form a non-thrombogenic monolayer.
candidates.credibility_concern: HIGHLY SATURATED — DESTROYED by JP5876173B2 (OrbusNeich) which directly teaches 'method for capturing progenitor endothelial cells using a drug-eluting stent'. This is the Genous/COMBO stent, a clinical product.

candidates.name: Mechanical anti-trauma feature (flexible neck / shock absorber)
candidates.core_mechanism: Flexible/segmented neck section between eShunt body and venous anchor that absorbs cardiac/respiratory pulsations and head movements, reducing mechanical trauma at the venous sinus interface.
candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Mechanical endothelial trauma, micro-motion-induced inflammation, anchor-site denudation
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: Compliant segment decouples anchor from main body, reducing stress concentration. Similar to flexible cardiac lead anchoring.
candidates.credibility: HIGH — cardiac lead anchoring and stent flexibility are mature engineering fields
candidates.credibility_concern: MEDIUM saturation — flexible stent bodies are well-known; eShunt-specific anatomical constraint (dural venous sinus ↔ subarachnoid space, brain pulsations + head movement) may distinguish.

candidates.name: Local nitric oxide (NO) generator (electrochemical or chemical)
candidates.core_mechanism: Miniature electrochemical or chemical NO generator integrated into eShunt that locally releases NO at venous interface to inhibit platelet aggregation and intimal hyperplasia.
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: NO activates soluble guanylate cyclase → ↑cGMP → smooth muscle relaxation + platelet inhibition. S-nitrosothiol polymers release NO via thermal/copper-catalyzed decomposition.
candidates.credibility: MEDIUM (implantable sustained NO generation) to HIGH (NO-releasing coatings)
candidates.credibility_concern: HIGHLY SATURATED — DESTROYED for surface-coating claims by 4 direct-hit patents: US8981139B2 (UNC), US10736996B2 (Chengdu SW Jiaotong), JP6763988B2 (Univ Michigan SNAP-doped), US20250236758A1 (Univ Georgia). NO-releasing implantable surfaces are saturated.

candidates.name: Bioresorbable protective outer layer (sacrificial sleeve on permanent eShunt)
candidates.core_mechanism: Bioresorbable polymer sleeve (e.g., PLGA, PCL, tyrosine polycarbonate) over the eShunt's venous-contacting surface that protects endothelium during initial deployment and early healing phase, then resorbs over 3-6 months leaving a clean permanent interface.
candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Deployment trauma, early thrombosis, acute inflammation, foreign-body reaction during critical healing window
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: Sacrificial layer cushions mechanical trauma during deployment; provides anti-thrombogenic surface during early healing; resorbs via hydrolytic/enzymatic degradation as endothelialization completes. PLGA degradation timeline tunable to 1-6 months.
candidates.credibility: MEDIUM-HIGH — bioresorbable scaffolds clinically validated (Abbott Absorb); sacrificial sleeves on permanent implants less common
candidates.credibility_concern: MEDIUM saturation — most prior art is FULLY bioresorbable scaffolds (Abbott Absorb, BVS). Sacrificial sleeve on PERMANENT implant is less saturated. Valentx US8968270B2 covers GI bypass sleeve replacement — different anatomy. eShunt-specific application novel.

candidates.name: Hydrodynamic buffer zone (recirculation region to distribute CSF drainage shear)
candidates.core_mechanism: Engineered multi-orifice distributor at the CSF-outflow tip that distributes CSF drainage across a wider impingement area on the venous sinus wall, preventing focal wall shear stress (WSS) hotspots from the CSF drainage jet.
candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Focal endothelial injury from CSF drainage jet, local intimal hyperplasia from WSS gradients
candidates.plausible_physical_principle: Multi-orifice distributor increases outflow area 5x → jet velocity decreases by sqrt(5) → impingement WSS decreases 5x. WSS gradient on venous sinus wall is the load-bearing metric for IH (Malek 1999).
candidates.credibility: MEDIUM — physics plausible per pre-check (Re_jet=10.5, transitional laminar; multi-orifice distributor geometrically feasible in 2mm axial length)
candidates.credibility_concern: HONEST NEGATIVE FINDING — physics pre-check (M10_PHYSICS_PRECHECK.json) revealed: at CSF flow 0.35 mL/min, the CSF jet's contribution to venous sinus wall WSS (~0.003 Pa focal, 0.0001 Pa distributed) is NEGLIGIBLE compared to venous blood flow WSS (~0.1-0.5 Pa normal, 1.0 Pa pathological). The CSF jet's contribution to total WSS is <3% of normal venous WSS. The mechanism's premise — that CSF drainage jet creates pathological focal WSS — DOES NOT HOLD UP. The leading-candidate pivot to M9 is driven by this honest negative finding.

step_5_first_attack.attack_target: M5 (Mechanical anti-trauma flexible neck) — strongest plausible alternative to M9
step_5_first_attack.attack_rationale: Per push-the-envelope doctrine: identify the strongest alternative to the leading candidate. If the alternative survives with simpler implementation, the leading candidate's complexity may not be justified. M5 is the strongest alternative because it addresses the same mechanical-trauma failure mode as M9 but with a permanent (non-resorbable) flexible feature.
step_5_first_attack.attack_statement: M5 (flexible neck) is the obvious choice for mechanical anti-trauma. Flexible stent bodies are well-known (coronary stents, peripheral stents, cardiac leads). M9 (bioresorbable sacrificial sleeve) adds complexity (degradation control, resorption byproducts, mechanical integrity throughout resorption) without clearly superior benefit. A PHOSITA would use a flexible neck.
defense_analysis: PARTIAL AGREEMENT: Flexible necks are well-known and M5 alone is not strongly novel.

DISTINCTION 1: eShunt bridges the dural venous sinus ↔ subarachnoid space — a unique anatomical transition where the dura mater is relatively rigid and the venous sinus moves with brain pulsations (~1Hz, 0.5-2 mm amplitude). Coronary stents handle only arterial pulsations (~1Hz, 0.1-0.3 mm amplitude). The amplitude difference is 5-10x. M5's flexible neck must accommodate this larger pulsation amplitude AND head movement — distinct from coronary stents.
DISTINCTION 2: M5 addresses MECHANICAL trauma only. M9 addresses MECHANICAL trauma (deployment) + BIOLOGICAL trauma (foreign-body reaction, early thrombosis). M9 is broader in scope.

DISTINCTION 3: M5's flexible feature is PERMANENT — long-term mechanical behavior must be characterized over 5-10+ years. M9's sacrificial sleeve is GONE in 3-6 months — long-term material characterization is not needed for the sleeve, only for the underlying eShunt.

DISTINCTION 4: M5 + M9 are not mutually exclusive — could be combined. But for V1 invention selection, M9 is preferred because (a) it addresses a broader failure mode set, (b) it has cleaner white space (sacrificial-on-permanent is less saturated than flexible-stent-bodies), (c) it has cleaner §101/§103 distinction (Valentx GI bypass vs eShunt venous interface is anatomy+mechanism).
step_5_first_attack.verdict: M9 SURVIVES ATTACK_1. M5 survives conditionally but is demoted to 'parallel candidate' status. M9 retains leading-candidate position based on broader failure-mode coverage and cleaner IP white space.
implications_for_V2: V2 should run ATTACK_2 (resorption byproduct biocompatibility) on M9.
V2 should run ATTACK_3 (premature sleeve failure during deployment) on M9.
V2 should evaluate M5 + M9 hybrid as a possible V2 alternative if M9 standalone fails any attack.
